# ReproMeta

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle:
experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-CMD-check](https://gitlab.uzh.ch/crsuzh/reprometa/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://gitlab.uzh.ch/crsuzh/reprometa/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

**_ReproMeta_** provides a unified R interface for assessing replication success
across several statistical interpretations of reproducibility, i.e.,
reproducibility metrics. *ReproMeta* allows meta-researchers to compute a whole 
set of reproducibility metrics systematically across the same set of original-
replication study pairs within a single and consistent workflow, without having
to rely on multiple packages and metric-specific implementations.

> Why does a unified interface matter?
  Metrics disagree in practice due to their underlying definitions, assumptions 
  and limitations (see DOI: <https://doi.org/10.1098/rsos.242076>). In Mita et 
  al. (2016 -- to appear), we systematically investigated the mathematical 
  deifnition, assumptions and limitation of known reproducibility metrics, and 
  established a unified mathematical notation to allow comparison. *ReproMeta* 
  provides the implementation of the metrics in R. This directly helps applied 
  researchers and meta-researchers to compute several of metrics side by side
  on the same study pair.
  
## Installation

ReproMeta is hosted on the UZH GitLab instance. To install the package, copy the following into your console:

```{r install-gitlab, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_gitlab("crsuzh/reprometa", host = "gitlab.uzh.ch")
```

## Usage -- quick start

```{r quickstart, eval = TRUE}
# After installation
library(ReproMeta)

# Prepare data
replication_data <- prepare_effect_sizes(r_o = 0.35, n_o = 100,
                                         r_r = 0.21, n_r = 120, 
                                         effectsize = "COR")

replication_results <- assess_replication_outcome(replication_data,
  metric = c("significance_r", "pScept", "BFr")
)

resqual <- get_replication_results(replication_results, type = "qualitative")
resquan <- get_replication_results(replication_results, type = "quantitative")
```

The qualitative results can be read of in the table below 
```{r table, eval = TRUE, echo=FALSE}
labels <- c(
  significance_r = "Significance criterion",
  pScept         = "Sceptical p-value (controlled)",
  BFr            = "Replication Bayes factor"
)

metrics <- sub("_outcome$", "", grep("_outcome$", names(resqual), value = TRUE))

long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(metrics, function(m) data.frame(
  study_id = resqual$study_id,
  metric   = m,
  outcome  = resqual[[paste0(m, "_outcome")]],
  detail   = resqual[[paste0(m, "_outcome_detailed")]],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)))

# ordered factor: controls both the label and the row order
long$metric <- factor(long$metric, levels = names(labels), labels = labels)
long <- long[order(long$study_id, long$metric), ]

knitr::kable(long, format = "html", row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Study", "Metric", "Outcome", "Details"))
```
